title.en: First day of mailing Vote by Mail ballots
title.es: Primer día de envío de boletas por correo

sub.en: Every registered voter in Alameda County is mailed a ballot (29 days before Election Day). Return envelope is postage-paid and must be signed.
sub.es: A cada votante registrado del Condado de Alameda se le envía una boleta (29 días antes del Día de la Elección). El sobre de devolución tiene franqueo pagado y debe estar firmado.

title.en: Early voting begins at the Registrar of Voters office; 24-hour drop boxes open
title.es: Comienza la votación anticipada en la oficina del Registro de Votantes; abren los buzones oficiales de 24 horas

sub.en: ROV office (1225 Fallon St): weekdays from Oct 5, 8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Sat Oct 31 and Sun Nov 1, 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Election Day 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. 66 official 24-hour drop boxes open Oct 5 until 8:00 p.m. on Nov 3.
sub.es: Oficina del Registro de Votantes (ROV) (1225 Fallon St): días de semana a partir del 5 de oct., 8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; sáb. 31 de oct. y dom. 1 de nov., 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Día de la Elección 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. 66 buzones oficiales de 24 horas abiertos desde el 5 de oct. hasta las 8:00 p.m. del 3 de nov.

title.en: Ballot Drop Stop tour begins (through Oct 30)
title.es: Comienza la gira Ballot Drop Stop (hasta el 30 de oct.)

sub.en: From Oct 30 through Nov 3 the Ballot Drop Stop is at 1225 Fallon St., Oakland. Tour stops listed at acvote.alamedacountyca.gov/dropstop (loaded dynamically).
sub.es: Del 30 de oct. al 3 de nov., el Ballot Drop Stop está en 1225 Fallon St., Oakland. Las paradas de la gira aparecen en acvote.alamedacountyca.gov/dropstop (se carga dinámicamente).

title.en: Close of voter registration (15 days before election)
title.es: Cierre del registro de votantes (15 días antes de la elección)

sub.en: Register online at registertovote.ca.gov or by paper form; voters who register after this date may need to vote at a Vote Center.
sub.es: Regístrese en línea en registertovote.ca.gov o con el formulario en papel; los votantes que se registren después de esta fecha podrían tener que votar en un centro de votación.

title.en: Conditional (same-day) voter registration available after the registration deadline
title.es: Registro condicional de votantes (el mismo día) disponible después de la fecha límite de registro

sub.en: County says eligible voters can conditionally register and vote at any Alameda County Vote Center after the Oct 19 deadline (through Election Day). Exact start day is not printed; date shown is the deadline after which it applies.
sub.es: El condado indica que los votantes elegibles pueden registrarse condicionalmente y votar en cualquier centro de votación del Condado de Alameda después de la fecha límite del 19 de oct. (hasta el Día de la Elección). El día exacto de inicio no está impreso; la fecha mostrada es la fecha límite después de la cual aplica.

title.en: First 20 Vote Centers open (county labels these "10-Day Vote Centers"; county pages elsewhere say 11 days)
title.es: Abren los primeros 20 centros de votación (el condado los denomina "10-Day Vote Centers"; otras páginas del condado dicen 11 días)

sub.en: 20 Vote Centers open Sat Oct 24-Mon Nov 2, 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., and Election Day Nov 3, 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Any voter may use any Vote Center.
sub.es: 20 centros de votación abren del sáb. 24 de oct. al lun. 2 de nov., 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., y el Día de la Elección, 3 de nov., 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Cualquier votante puede usar cualquier centro de votación.

title.en: Last day to request a replacement Vote by Mail ballot (to be mailed); also the county's recommended last day to mail a ballot
title.es: Último día para solicitar una boleta por correo de reemplazo (para que se envíe por correo); también es el último día que el condado recomienda para enviar una boleta por correo

sub.en: Request via (510) 272-6973 or the online form. VIG p.2 advises mailing the ballot by Oct 27 so it is received in time to be processed.
sub.es: Solicítela al (510) 272-6973 o mediante el formulario en línea. La Guía de Información para el Votante (VIG), p.2, aconseja enviar la boleta por correo a más tardar el 27 de oct. para que se reciba a tiempo para ser procesada.

title.en: 80 additional Vote Centers open ("4-Day Vote Centers"; 100 total)
title.es: Abren 80 centros de votación adicionales ("4-Day Vote Centers"; 100 en total)

sub.en: Open Sat Oct 31-Mon Nov 2, 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., and Election Day 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.
sub.es: Abiertos del sáb. 31 de oct. al lun. 2 de nov., 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., y el Día de la Elección 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.

sub.en: All Vote Centers open 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; 24-hour drop boxes close at 8:00 p.m.; results posted shortly after 8:00 p.m.
sub.es: Todos los centros de votación abren 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; los buzones oficiales de 24 horas cierran a las 8:00 p.m.; los resultados se publican poco después de las 8:00 p.m.

title.en: Deadline for mailed ballots to arrive (must be postmarked on or before Nov 3)
title.es: Fecha límite para que lleguen las boletas enviadas por correo (deben tener sello postal del 3 de nov. o antes)

sub.en: Ballots returned in person must be received by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
sub.es: Las boletas entregadas en persona deben recibirse a más tardar a las 8:00 p.m. del Día de la Elección.

gaps: Statewide propositions are on the ballot (the county VIG sample ballot shows them) but were not extracted, per instructions. They are in the State Voter Information Guide (voterguide.sos.ca.gov).

Judicial retention contests (California Supreme Court and First District Court of Appeal justices; e.g., Justice Joshua Groban) appear on the county sample ballot in the VIG but are not on the county Candidate List, so they were not extracted. They are in the obfuscated-font sample ballot pages of the VIG PDF (pdf pages ~40 onward).

No Alameda County offices (Board of Supervisors, DA, Sheriff, Assessor, County Superintendent of Schools, Superior Court) are on the Nov 3 list: the county candidate list for election 260 has only Federal, State, School Districts, Special Districts and City categories, while the June 2 primary list (election 259) had County, Supervisor and Superior Court categories. So there are no county runoffs on this ballot. (Inference from category lists; the county does not state it.)
Term lengths are not printed in the county list except "Short Term" / "Full Term" in some titles; `term` is null elsewhere (not filled from outside knowledge).

The county list's Incumbent flag is unreliable (31 "Y" vs 235 "N"; several sitting officeholders, e.g., Rep. Lateefah Simon, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Mayor Barbara Lee, are flagged "N"). `incumbent` is true only where the list says Y and null otherwise; the raw flag is in `incumbent_listed`. Ballot designations such as "Incumbent" appear verbatim in `ballot_designation`.
30 races are marked "Not On Ballot" on the county list (35 Filing-Completed candidates) and are in `not_on_ballot_contests`, not `contests`. The county does not state the reason.

Peralta Community College District Trustee, Area 1, Short Term is listed by the county as an office on the ballot, but the candidate list returns no candidate rows for it (no seats/vote-for value either).

10 filings on the county list are not "Filing Completed" and are excluded from candidates: 5 in on-ballot contests (Candidacy Withdrawn: Kate Runyon, Linda Hurley; Incomplete Filing: Mark Williams, Heriberto Perez, Shanavaz Nasarabadi) kept under `not_qualified_filings`, and 5 in not-on-ballot contests (Mike McMahon withdrawn; Tonya Arledge, Barbara Armstrong, Jonathan Leder, Jason Matthew Miguel incomplete). None of the five on-ballot ones appears on the VIG sample ballot.

County measures list prints "Percentage Passing: N/A" for Measures RTM, J, K, BB. Thresholds for these were filled from the county VIG (RTM majority district-wide, J two-thirds, K 55 percent, BB majority) and flagged with `threshold_src`.

Registrar phone is inconsistent across county pages: (510) 272-6973 (site footer, VIG help line) vs (510) 272-6933 (About Us page, VIG letterhead and Measure J analysis); toolkit FAQ lists (510) 272-6982, which the footer gives as the fax number. Both 6973 and 6933 are recorded.

Per-address sample ballots are only available through the voter-login Voter Profile; the composite VIG PDF is the public sample. Vote center list was pulled from the county list fragment (100 centers); the drop-box map is JavaScript/Google Maps and its page text is a stale 2020 copy, so the 66 drop boxes were taken from VIG pages 9-11. Dropbox/vote-center lists are marked "subject to change" by the county.
Ballot Drop Stop tour dates/locations load dynamically and were not retrieved.
Candidate statements were not extracted; they are Tab 4 of the VIG PDF (pages after the sample ballots, roughly pdf pp. 300-750).

San Leandro RCV status is ambiguous: county RCV page lists San Leandro among RCV cities, but the Nov 3 2026 sample ballot shows San Leandro contests as standard contests. `rcv` is null for San Leandro contests.

Source-data quirks: Albany Council candidate Aaron Tiedemann has Filing Agency "City of Alameda"; Measure L question text has an encoding artifact (normalized to an em dash); the county lists the same person in several contests (Joseph Grcar 6 contests, Luis Reynoso 3, Joe Orlando Ramos 2).
Candidate List page carries no posting timestamp ("current as of the date posted"); fetched 2026-10-08 (election nominations closed Aug 7, 2026).

Wayback Machine was not needed: all acvote.alamedacountyca.gov and alamedacountyca.gov pages above returned HTTP 200. The guessed path www.acvote.org/elections/ returned 404; www.acvote.org redirects to acvote.alamedacountyca.gov.

No county page found that maps ballot types (BT1..BT263 in the VIG) to cities, areas or precincts; the county GIS Consolidated Precincts layer has only Precinct_ID. ballot_styles.json therefore has empty `areas`; the footer precinct number of each sample ballot is recorded as `sample_precinct_id`.

election.es: Elección general del 3 de noviembre de 2026

summary.en: Housing emergency, price-gouging crackdown, lower drug prices.
summary.es: Emergencia de vivienda, freno a precios abusivos, medicinas más baratas.

background.en: Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services; former California Attorney General.
background.es: Ex secretario de Salud de EE. UU.; ex fiscal general de California.

statement.en: Declare the housing shortage a state emergency; reform building fees statewide.
statement.es: Declarar emergencia estatal por la escasez de vivienda; reformar las tarifas de construcción.

statement.en: Stand up to price gouging and unjustified rate hikes; expand child-care help.
statement.es: Enfrentar precios abusivos y alzas injustificadas; ampliar ayuda para cuidado infantil.

statement.en: Protect everyone’s coverage; negotiate lower drug prices for state programs.
statement.es: Proteger la cobertura de todos; negociar medicinas más baratas en programas estatales.

summary.en: No income tax on first $150K, $3 gas, starter homes.
summary.es: Sin impuesto sobre los primeros $150K, gasolina a $3, casas iniciales.

background.en: Former senior adviser to a British prime minister; former Fox News host.
background.es: Ex asesor de un primer ministro británico; ex presentador de Fox News.

statement.en: No state income tax on the first $150,000 you earn.
statement.es: Sin impuesto estatal sobre los primeros $150,000 que ganes.

statement.en: End the rules and fees behind high gas prices; cut utility bills in half.
statement.es: Eliminar las reglas y tarifas que encarecen la gasolina; reducir a la mitad las facturas de servicios.

statement.en: Clear red tape and fees so starter homes for young families get built.
statement.es: Eliminar trabas y tarifas para que se construyan casas iniciales para familias jóvenes.

juris.en: Public Transit Revenue Measure District (Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, Santa Clara counties and City and County of San Francisco)
juris.es: Public Transit Revenue Measure District (Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, Santa Clara counties and City and County of San Francisco)

local_measures.title: Regional Transit Measure
local_measures.question: To prevent major service cuts to BART and other transit, avoid increased traffic, and reduce pollution by: Preserving BART, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, AC Transit, Muni, other transit for everyone, including workers, students, seniors, persons with disabilities; Supporting transit safety, cleanliness, affordability, reliability; Repairing targeted roads/potholes; Requiring financial transparency, oversight, accountability; shall the measure enacting a 0.5% (Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, Santa Clara counties), and 1% (San Francisco) sales tax for 14 years generating approximately $980,000,000 annually, be adopted?
local_measures.threshold: Majority of those voting on the measure district-wide (Public Transit Revenue Measure District)

local_measures.title: Parcel Tax Measure
local_measures.question: "Shall the measure to support quality education, provide local funding that cannot be taken by the State, maintain small class sizes, attract/retain quality teachers, and provide enhanced science, technology, engineering, visual and performing arts, reading, writing, and math programs, by renewing the expiring $96 school parcel tax, adding $48 per parcel, providing approximately $2,900,000 annually for nine years, with senior exemptions, annual inflation adjustments, independent oversight, and all funds locally controlled, be adopted?"

local_measures.title: Education Parcel Tax Measure
local_measures.question: "To renew expiring local school funding without increasing current tax rates; support academic excellence and programs in reading, writing, math, arts, science and technology; attract and retain highly qualified teachers and staff; and continue stable, local funding the State cannot take away; shall San Lorenzo Unified School District's measure be adopted, renewing its expiring $99 parcel tax for 12 years, providing approximately $1.8 million annually, with senior exemptions, citizen oversight, and no funds for district administrators?"
local_measures.threshold: Two-thirds of qualified electors voting on the measure

local_measures.title: GO Bond Measure
local_measures.question: To improve the quality of local education; complete the Main Building retrofit and renovation; replace deteriorating plumbing, electrical, sewer, heating and ventilation systems; and modernize and upgrade old classrooms and restrooms; shall Sunol Glen Unified School District's measure be adopted authorizing $6,100,000 of bonds at legal rates, generating on average $431,700 annually while bonds are outstanding at approximate rates of $35 per $100,000 assessed value, with audits, citizens' oversight, no money for salaries and funds staying local?
local_measures.threshold: At least 55 percent of voters voting on the measure

local_measures.title: GO Bond Measure
local_measures.question: SAFER Alameda Act — Preparing Alameda for Sea-Level Rise, Accidents, Flooding, Earthquakes, Resilience. To prepare for emergencies, earthquakes and sea-level rise; prevent flooded Tubes; repair potholes; keep streets safe and accessible; maintain response to fires, accidents, and medical emergencies; prevent Bay pollution; and protect shorelines; shall the City of Alameda measure issuing $300,000,000 in bonds, levying $49/$100,000 of assessed value, generating approximately $19,000,000 annually while bonds are outstanding, requiring oversight, public disclosures, and local control, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Charter Amendment - Amend And Repeal Outdated Provisions
local_measures.question: Proposed City Charter Amendment Ballot Measure Shall the measure amending City Charter Sections 2-1.1, 2-3, 2-10, 3-7(G), 3-14, 7-2(J), 8-2, 8-5, 10-3, 10-6, 10-7, 10-12, 12-4(A) and (B), 14-1, 17-10, 28-2, 28-3 and 28-4, and repealing Sections 12-3(D) and 23-3 to conform to existing practices and amend and repeal outdated provisions be adopted?

local_measures.title: Charter Amendment - Leases And Sales Of Real Property Measure
local_measures.question: Proposed City Charter Amendment Ballot Measure Shall the measure amending Section 3-10 of the City Charter to change sales or leases of City real property exceeding one year to be approved by resolution rather than by ordinance and to reduce the City Council approval threshold from supermajority (four affirmative votes) to simple majority (three affirmative votes) for leases of City real property not exceeding ten years be adopted?

local_measures.title: Requirement To Zoning Changes Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure authorizing the Albany City Council to amend the residential voter requirements for zoning changes to the R-1 zoned areas of the City established by Measure D (enacted by the Albany voters in 1978), without majority neighborhood voter approval, after following noticed public hearing and zoning ordinance amendment procedures prescribed by State Law and the Albany Municipal Code, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Street Paving And Storm Drain Parcel Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure updating the Street Paving and Storm Drain Special Tax, by adding very low-income rebates and low-income tax exemptions and rebates; applying the tax to possessory interests; and if a parcel over 500,000 square feet becomes exempt from this tax, adjusting the rate from $167.65 per equivalent residential unit to $0.0638 per lot square foot as provided in the measure, providing an estimated $1,400,000 annually until ended by voters, be adopted?

local_measures.title: EMS, ALS, Fire Protection Parcel Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure updating the Emergency Medical Services, Advanced Life Support, and Fire Protection Special Tax on residential and commercial property, by adding low-income tax exemptions and rebates, and adjusting the rate from $0.0807 per square foot to the new rates as provided in the measure if a parcel over 500,000 square feet in size becomes exempt from this tax, providing an estimated $2,500,000 annually until ended by voters, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Business License Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure supporting City of Albany general services, such as fire protection, public safety, environmental and community service programs, by increasing the City's business license tax to those rates specified in the measure, levying the tax upon business gross receipts instead of number of employees, and updating local tax collection procedures, providing an estimated additional $600,000 annually, until ended by voters, with all funds remaining local which cannot be taken by Sacramento be adopted?

local_measures.title: Real Property Transfer Tax Measure
local_measures.question: To support City of Albany general services, with funding that cannot be taken by Sacramento, including: street and park maintenance, recreation, public safety, and environmental programs, shall a measure adjusting the City's real property transfer tax rate from $15.00 to between $10.00 and $30.00 per $1,000 purchased, depending upon the property's purchase price, providing an additional $1,000,000 annually, until ended by voters, with all funds remaining local be adopted?

local_measures.title: Street Trees & Streetlighting Parcel Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure to enact a special parcel tax on non-exempt property in the City at $0.0354 per lot square foot to maintain and improve public street trees and streetlighting to enhance local safety and sustainability, subject to an annual consumer price index adjustment up to 3%, exempting qualifying low-income residents, providing an estimated $775,000 annually until ended by voters, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Bond Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure authorizing issuance of $300,000,000 in general obligation bonds to fund acquisition and improvement of fire stations, emergency response facilities, parks and recreation facilities, and other public infrastructure and facilities, and increase climate resiliency, subject to independent oversight and audits, be adopted? Financial Implications: Average annual taxpayer costs over projected 40 years bonds are outstanding are approximately $22.14 per $100,000 assessed property value; generating approximately $15,200,000/year.

local_measures.title: Sales Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure levying a 0.5% sales tax in Berkeley, increasing the total sales tax rate in the City to 10.75%, estimated to generate $9,000,000 to $10,000,000 annually, with proceeds placed into the General Fund for general City uses, including but not limited to sustaining fire, police and 911 dispatch services, youth and senior services, and community programs, until ended by the voters, with independent audits, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Charter Amendment Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure amending the City Charter to reduce candidate filing fees; eliminate signatures in lieu of filing fee process; eliminate certain personal information from candidate statements; clarify and revise initiative, referendum and recall processes; amend election timelines for filling Mayor and Councilmember vacancies; increase the maximum amount from the public campaign financing fund for administration and enforcement from $250,000 to $400,000 per four-year election cycle; and make other changes be adopted?

local_measures.title: Rent Ordinance Amendment Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure to amend the Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance by making most rent control and registration exemptions inapplicable to units that were not exempt when the current tenancy began; allowing modification or waiver of fees for subsidized units owned or leased by nonprofits; changing the annual registration deadline; limiting annual rent increases to ten percent; and allowing tenant associations in smaller properties, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Initiative - Arts Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure creating a special parcel tax to fund grants for performing arts organizations, art projects, art organization operational and programmatic expenses and capital projects, community festivals, and administrative costs, with oversight by the City's Civic Arts Commission, at a rate of $0.07 per square foot of improvements, estimated to generate approximately $6,300,000 annually and $84,800,000 over its twelve-year duration, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Initiative - Public Bank Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure creating a special parcel tax to capitalize and support a public bank to fund investments in affordable housing, green energy/infrastructure and small businesses, at rates of $0.06/square foot of residential improvements and $0.09/square foot of non-residential improvements, estimated to generate approximately $9,200,000 the first year and $58,300,000 over its six-year duration, with funds subject to review, allocation and approval by the City Council and regular audits, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Initiative - Soda Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure replacing the City's $0.01 per fluid ounce general tax on the distribution of sugar-sweetened beverages with a $0.02 per fluid ounce special tax to fund public health, nutrition, and drinking water accessibility programs by nonprofits, the City, or Berkeley Unified School District, retaining current exemptions for small retailers, milk products, baby formula, alcoholic beverages, and medical and weight-loss products, estimated to generate approximately $2,200,000 annually, until repealed by the voters, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Business Tax Measure
local_measures.question: City Services/ Business License Reform Measure. "To protect City of Emeryville services/ensure smaller businesses pay less than larger businesses, shall the measure be adopted to: keep parks/playgrounds safe; repair potholes/maintain streets; maintain 9-1-1 response; improve crime prevention; maintain senior/youth services; general government use; by updating/simplifying Emeryville's 42 year old business license rates up to 0.4% of gross receipts (described in the ordinance) until ended by voters, providing $12,400,000 annually, requiring independent oversight?"

local_measures.title: Business Tax Measure
local_measures.question: HAYWARD BUSINESS LICENSE TAX MODERNIZATION: Shall the measure updating the Hayward Business License Tax for the first time since 1978, to support general city services, including neighborhood police protection, firefighting, 911 response, libraries, and pothole repair, generating an additional $12 million annually until repealed, with a minimum tax of $60 and rates from $.30 to $3.75 per $1,000 of gross receipts, with higher rates for higher-grossing businesses, as stated in the ordinance, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Newark Essential Services Protection Measure
local_measures.question: "Newark Essential Services Protection Measure. To protect city services such as repairing potholes/streets; keeping neighborhoods safe/clean, and maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response/fire protection/neighborhood police patrols/parks/recreation programs, shall the measure be adopted updating Newark's 56-year-old business license ordinance, lowering many small businesses' taxes, with rates up to 0.3% of gross receipts (as described in the ordinance), raising $6,600,000 annually until ended by voters, with spending disclosure/independent audits?"

local_measures.title: Charter Amendment Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure to amend Oakland's City Charter to, among other things, (1) make the Mayor the City's chief executive with a legislative veto, (2) empower the Council to override vetoes, confirm appointments of certain directors, and appoint an Independent Budget and Legislative Analyst, (3) affirm Councilmembers' right to acquire information from other City officials, (4) require Councilmembers to work full-time, and (5) empower the Public Ethics Commission to set salaries for all City elected officials using similar formulas, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Real Property Tax
local_measures.question: Shall the measure amending Oakland's Real Property Transfer Tax Ordinance to eliminate the foreclosure exception for all property transfers except transfers converting commercial property to certain housing or healthcare uses, transfers to community banking organizations, and certain transfers of residential properties of four units or less, and allowing the City Council to establish, amend, or remove foreclosure-related exceptions, raising approximately $4-$13 million annually pursuant to tax rates in Oakland Municipal Code section 4.20.020, beginning January 1, 2027 until repealed, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Real Property Conveyance Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall the measure, providing funding for City of Piedmont's essential city services, such as police, fire, and emergency medical response; and maintenance of aging City buildings, parks, stormwater drains, roads and sidewalks, by increasing the real estate transfer tax from 1.3% to 1.75% to be more in line with neighboring cities and to generate approximately $1,500,000 annually in general tax revenue until ended by voters, be adopted?

local_measures.title: Uniform Transient Occupancy Tax Measure
local_measures.question: Shall a measure be adopted to increase the City's Uniform Transient Occupancy Tax paid by hotel guests from 8% to 10% on July 1, 2027, and to 12% on July 1, 2028, generating an estimated $1.4 to $2.8 million per year in additional revenue, that can be used to maintain city services, such as: police and fire protection; park and street maintenance; recreation programs; and other general government uses, until ended by voters?

local_measures.title: Union City Essential Services Extension Measure
local_measures.question: "Union City Essential Services Extension Measure. To maintain critical city services, including 9-1-1 emergency response/paramedics/fire protection; street/pothole repair; neighborhood police patrols; crime/gun violence prevention programs; youth/senior programs; and other city services, shall the measure extending the City of Union City's existing voter-approved utility users tax for 9 years at the current 5% rate (no increase), providing $7,000,000 annually, with senior/low-income exemptions, annual audits, and all funds locally controlled, be adopted?"
